key_insight: Photon-drag currents in altermagnets split into domain-even and domain-odd angular harmonics, letting light reveal the Néel domain and symmetry of the magnetic order.
engineering_relevance: This suggests an all-optical, symmetry-based readout method for magnetic domain states, potentially useful for noncontact device diagnostics and spintronic materials characterization.
method: Analyze second-order photocurrents driven by finite photon momentum in centrosymmetric altermagnets.
Compare angular harmonics under 90° sample rotations to separate domain-even (4n) and domain-odd (4n+2) components.
Use polarization-dependent selection rules to identify which microscopic current terms are domain odd.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports symmetry-resolved theoretical analysis showing that linear light makes only the shift term domain odd, while circular light shifts domain oddness to injection, Fermi-surface, and contact principal-value terms.
watch_item: The proposed charge-current readout requires spin-orbit coupling to be observable, so materials with weak SOC may give a much smaller or undetectable signal.
paper_title: Reading Altermagnetic Domains with Photon Drag
